gloss_modern: This means noticing good things received, from people or chance, and expressing thanks rather than taking them for granted.
reasoning: Gratitude is awareness of and thankfulness for good things received. The grateful person of today notices favors from others or from chance and feels appreciation rather than taking them for granted.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: gratitude used too little, or not at all, where it would serve
gloss_modern: This means taking benefits for granted and feeling no thanks toward others, insisting one owes nothing to anyone.
reasoning: Rugged individualism is gratitude used too little: the person feels no thanks toward those who helped and insists they owe nothing to anyone.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: gratitude used too much, past the point where it serves
gloss_modern: This means flattering and deferring to others so excessively that one's thanks turns servile and aimed at winning favor.
reasoning: Ingratiation is gratitude used too much: the person flatters and defers to others so lavishly, aiming to win favor, that their thanks becomes servile.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: expecting the best in the future and working to achieve it
gloss_modern: This means expecting good outcomes in the future and working toward them, keeping heart when things look difficult.
reasoning: Hope is expecting the best in the future and working to achieve it. The hopeful person of today keeps heart when things look hard and acts to bring good outcomes about.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: hope used too little, or not at all, where it would serve
gloss_modern: This means expecting the worst from the future and doubting that effort will matter, so one often gives up before trying.
reasoning: Negativism is hope used too little: the person expects the worst from the future and doubts that effort will matter, so often gives up before trying.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: hope used too much, past the point where it serves
gloss_modern: This means expecting everything to turn out well regardless of evidence, ignoring risks and so failing to prepare for trouble.
reasoning: Pollyanna-ism is hope used too much: the person expects everything to turn out well regardless of evidence, ignoring risks and so failing to prepare for trouble.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: liking to laugh and tease; bringing smiles to other people
gloss_modern: This means enjoying laughter and good-natured teasing, lightening moods and bringing smiles to others through wit.
reasoning: Humor here means enjoying laughter and teasing and bringing smiles to others. The humorous person of today lightens moods with wit and good-natured fun.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: humor used too little, or not at all, where it would serve
gloss_modern: This means taking things so gravely that a light touch goes unused, even where a joke would ease tension or help.
reasoning: Humor is the strength; its underuse, called over-seriousness, is a person who withholds lightness even where it would ease tension or help. Today we would call them humorless.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: humor used too much, past the point where it serves
gloss_modern: This means joking constantly and at inappropriate moments, turning every occasion into a jest, even when it spoils serious matters.
reasoning: Giddiness is humor used past the point of usefulness, so the person jokes and clowns constantly, even when the moment calls for seriousness. Today we would call them frivolous.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: having coherent beliefs about the higher purpose and meaning of life
gloss_modern: This means holding a settled sense of life's larger purpose, and letting that conviction guide how one lives and treats others.
reasoning: This is a person with a settled, coherent view of life's higher purpose and meaning, which guides how they live. Today we would call them spiritual, though the word has other senses.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: spirituality used too little, or not at all, where it would serve
gloss_modern: This means lacking any coherent sense of life's larger purpose, so one drifts without beliefs or values to steer by.
reasoning: Anomie is the underuse of spirituality: a person without any coherent beliefs about life's purpose or meaning, so they drift without guiding values. Today we would call them adrift or rootless.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: spirituality used too much, past the point where it serves
gloss_modern: This means clinging to one's beliefs with blind intensity, pressing them on others, and refusing any doubt or compromise.
reasoning: Fanaticism is spirituality carried past reason, so the person clings to beliefs with blind intensity and will not tolerate doubt. Today we would call them fanatical.
source: Niemiec (2019), 'Finding the golden mean: the overuse, underuse, and optimal use of character strengths', Counselling Psychology Quarterly 32(3-4), 453-471, doi:10.1080/09515070.2019.1617674, Table 1 (paywalled, not read at verification); the labels are the noun nomenclature of Freidlin, Littman-Ovadia & Niemiec (2017), 'Positive psychopathology: social anxiety via character strengths underuse and overuse', Personality and Individual Differences 108, 50-54, Table 1 (which credits it to Niemiec 2014)

gloss: a strong need for submitting passively to others, accepting blame, criticism and punishment, confessing faults
gloss_modern: This means yielding to others, accepting criticism and blame readily, and confessing faults, sometimes even seeking correction or punishment.
reasoning: This person has a strong need to submit to others and accept blame, criticism and punishment, confessing faults readily. Today we would call them submissive.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: rarely submitting or accepting blame; resisting criticism
gloss_modern: This means refusing to yield, rarely admitting fault, and pushing back against criticism rather than accepting blame or correction.
reasoning: This person rarely submits or accepts blame and resists criticism. Today we would call them defiant.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for accomplishing something difficult, mastering obstacles, excelling and rivaling others
gloss_modern: This means pursuing difficult goals, overcoming obstacles, and wanting to excel, often measuring oneself against rivals.
reasoning: This person has a strong drive to accomplish difficult things, master obstacles and excel over rivals. Today we would call them ambitious.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little drive to accomplish or excel; content with ordinary results
gloss_modern: This means feeling little drive to excel or accomplish more, and being quite content with ordinary results and modest goals.
reasoning: This person has little drive to excel and is content with ordinary results. Today we would call them unambitious.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for drawing close to others, forming friendships and winning affection
gloss_modern: This means seeking close company, forming friendships readily, and wanting warm affection from others, feeling lonely without them.
reasoning: This person strongly wants close company, friendships and affection from others. Today we would call them sociable.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish for company or friendship; content to be alone
gloss_modern: This means preferring to be alone, with little wish for company or close friendships, and staying content without much social contact.
reasoning: This person has little wish for company or friendship and is content to be alone. Today we would call them solitary.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for overcoming opposition forcefully, fighting, attacking or belittling others
gloss_modern: This means forcing one's will against opposition, readily fighting, attacking, or belittling others in order to win and dominate.
reasoning: This person has a strong need to overcome opposition by force, fighting, attacking or belittling others. Today we would call them combative.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to fight or attack; avoiding confrontation
gloss_modern: This means avoiding confrontation and fights, letting disputes pass rather than pressing them forcefully against others.
reasoning: This person has little wish to fight or attack and avoids confrontation. Today we would call them peaceable.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for being free of restraint, acting independently and resisting coercion
gloss_modern: This means resisting restraint and coercion, insisting on acting by one's own choices, and wanting freedom from others' direction.
reasoning: This person strongly needs freedom from restraint, acts on their own choices and resists coercion. Today we would call them independent.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little need for independence; content to follow rules and others' direction
gloss_modern: This means willingly following rules and others' direction, with little need for independence and happy to let others decide.
reasoning: This person has little need for independence and is content to follow rules and others' direction. Today we would call them compliant.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for mastering or making up for a failure by trying again, overcoming weakness
gloss_modern: This means picking oneself up after failure, retrying, and working to overcome one's weaknesses rather than accepting defeat.
reasoning: This person strongly wants to make up for failure by trying again and overcoming their weaknesses. Today we would call them resilient.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little drive to retry after failure; accepting defeat
gloss_modern: This means accepting setbacks as final, with little drive to retry or make up for losses, and readily giving up.
reasoning: This person has little drive to retry after failure and simply accepts defeat. Today we would call them defeatist.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for defending oneself against attack, criticism and blame, justifying oneself
gloss_modern: This means hastily justifying oneself whenever criticized or blamed, guarding against any suggestion of fault, and bristling at challenge.
reasoning: This person strongly needs to defend themselves against criticism and blame and to justify their conduct. Today we would call them defensive.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little need to justify or defend oneself against criticism
gloss_modern: This means shrugging off criticism and blame without feeling compelled to justify oneself, letting faultfinding pass undefended.
reasoning: This person feels little need to justify or defend themselves against criticism. Today we would call them thick-skinned.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for admiring and supporting a superior, praising and conforming to custom
gloss_modern: This means admiring and supporting those above one, praising them readily, and following custom and convention rather than challenging it.
reasoning: This person strongly needs to admire and support superiors, praise them, and conform to custom. Today we would call them deferential.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to admire or follow superiors; unimpressed by rank
gloss_modern: This means they feel little urge to admire or follow superiors and are unimpressed by status.
reasoning: Deference is the wish to admire and follow superiors. Someone with a low need for it feels little pull toward rank and judges authorities on their merits, so today they would be called independent-minded.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for controlling one's human environment, directing and influencing others
gloss_modern: This means they strongly want to direct others, steer decisions, and shape the people and events around them.
reasoning: Dominance is the need to control one's surroundings and direct others. A person with a high need for it wants to lead, steer decisions and influence people, which we would call dominant or controlling.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to control or direct others
gloss_modern: This means they feel little wish to control others and are happy to let others take the lead.
reasoning: A low need for dominance means little wish to direct others. Such a person is content to let others lead and is easy to work with, which we would call accommodating.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for making an impression, being seen and heard, entertaining and shocking
gloss_modern: This means they crave being noticed and heard, and enjoy entertaining or startling others to make an impression.
reasoning: Exhibition is the need to make an impression and be seen and heard. A person with a high need for it performs, entertains and shocks to be noticed, which we call attention-seeking.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to be noticed; avoiding attention
gloss_modern: This means they shun the spotlight and would rather go unnoticed than be seen or heard.
reasoning: A low need for exhibition means avoiding attention and preferring not to be watched. Today we would call such a person unassuming or self-effacing.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for avoiding pain, injury and danger, taking precautions
gloss_modern: This means they go to considerable lengths to avoid pain, injury and danger, taking many precautions.
reasoning: Harm avoidance is the need to escape pain, injury and danger by taking precautions. A person with a high need for it is careful and wary, which we call risk-averse or cautious.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little concern with avoiding danger or injury
gloss_modern: This means they pay little heed to danger or injury and readily take risks others would avoid.
reasoning: A low need for harm avoidance means little concern with danger or injury. Such a person takes chances readily, which we call daring or fearless.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for avoiding humiliation, embarrassment and failure, refraining from action for fear of it
gloss_modern: This means they dread humiliation and failure so much that they often hold back rather than risk acting.
reasoning: Infavoidance is the need to avoid humiliation, embarrassment and failure, even by not acting. A person with a high need for it holds back to protect their pride, which we call failure-averse or shame-avoidant.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little fear of embarrassment or failure
gloss_modern: This means they are little troubled by embarrassment or failure and act without fear of looking foolish.
reasoning: A low need for infavoidance means little fear of embarrassment or failure. Such a person acts boldly and shrugs off looking foolish, which we call unembarrassable or undaunted.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for giving sympathy and help to the helpless, feeding, protecting and comforting
gloss_modern: This means they feel a strong pull to comfort, feed and protect those who are weak, young, or in need.
reasoning: Nurturance is the need to sympathize with, feed, protect and comfort the helpless. A person with a high need for it is drawn to caring for others, which we call nurturing.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to care for or help the helpless
gloss_modern: This means they feel little urge to help or comfort the helpless and keep their distance from others' needs.
reasoning: A low need for nurturance means little wish to care for the helpless. Such a person keeps a distance from others' dependence and is not drawn to comforting them, which we call detached.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for putting things in order, achieving cleanliness, arrangement and precision
gloss_modern: This means they strongly crave tidiness, arrangement and precision, and feel uneasy when things are untidy.
reasoning: The need for order is the drive for arrangement, cleanliness and precision. A person with a high need for it keeps things tidy and exact, which we call orderly or meticulous.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little need for order or neatness; tolerant of mess
gloss_modern: This means they tolerate mess and disarray easily and feel little need for neatness or precision.
reasoning: A low need for order means little concern for neatness and tolerance of mess. Today we would call such a person untidy or careless of order.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for acting for fun without further purpose, laughing and joking, seeking relaxation
gloss_modern: This means they seek fun for its own sake, laugh and joke often, and look for ways to relax.
reasoning: The need for play is the wish to act for fun without further purpose and to joke and relax. A person with a high need for it is light-hearted and fun-loving, which we call playful.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish for fun or play; serious and work-bound
gloss_modern: This means they seldom seek fun for its own sake and tend to focus on work and duty.
reasoning: A low need for play means little wish for fun and a focus on work. Such a person is earnest and businesslike, which we call serious-minded.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for separating oneself from people one dislikes, excluding, snubbing and jilting them
gloss_modern: This means they readily cut off, exclude or snub people they dislike, pushing them out of their circle.
reasoning: Rejection is the need to separate from disliked people by excluding, snubbing or dropping them. A person with a high need for it cuts people off, which we call shunning or dismissive.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to exclude or snub others; accepting of most people
gloss_modern: This means they rarely exclude or snub anyone and get along with most people they meet.
reasoning: A low need for rejection means little wish to exclude or snub anyone. Such a person is tolerant and welcoming, which we call inclusive and accepting.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for seeking and enjoying sensuous impressions
gloss_modern: This means they actively seek out and savor sensory pleasures such as taste, touch, sound and beauty.
reasoning: The need for sentience is the drive to seek and enjoy sensory impressions. A person with a high need for it savors taste, touch, sound and sight, which we call sensual or sensation-seeking.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little interest in sensuous pleasures
gloss_modern: This means they take little interest in sensory pleasures and can do without rich food, music, or touch.
reasoning: A low need for sentience means little interest in sensory pleasures. Such a person is content without rich food, music or physical comfort, which we call austere.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for forming and furthering an erotic relationship
gloss_modern: This means they strongly pursue erotic relationships and invest much energy in romantic and sexual attachment.
reasoning: The need for sex is the drive to form and further an erotic relationship. A person with a high need for it pursues romantic and sexual attachment with energy, which we call amorous.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little sexual interest
gloss_modern: This means having little interest in sex, showing little drive toward sexual pursuit or physical intimacy.
reasoning: Murray's low pole for sex marks someone with a weak drive toward sexual pleasure or contact. Today such a person is simply sexually uninterested, with little appetite for sexual activity.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for having one's needs met by a sympathetic other, being nursed, supported and protected
gloss_modern: This means constantly seeking comfort, support and protection from others, wanting to be looked after when troubled.
reasoning: Succorance is the need to be nursed, supported and protected by a sympathetic other. A person with a strong need for it today is someone who leans heavily on others for comfort and reassurance.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little wish to be helped or comforted; self-reliant in trouble
gloss_modern: This means handling difficulties on one's own, neither wanting nor seeking help, comfort or reassurance from others.
reasoning: The low pole of succorance describes someone who feels little wish to be helped or comforted and copes with trouble alone. Today we call such a person self-reliant.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: a strong need for asking and answering general questions, interested in theory, analysis and generalization
gloss_modern: This means constantly asking general questions and enjoying theory, analysis, and drawing broad conclusions from particular facts.
reasoning: Murray's high need for understanding is a drive to ask general questions and pursue theory, analysis and generalization. Today this person is analytical and intellectually inquisitive.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs

gloss: little interest in theory or in understanding why
gloss_modern: This means showing little interest in explanations or theory, taking things at face value without asking why they happen.
reasoning: The low pole of understanding describes someone with little interest in theory or in grasping why things are as they are. Today we would call such a person incurious about ideas and explanations.
source: Murray (1938), Explorations in Personality: the twenty manifest needs
